title: Database Developer (PL/SQL)
summary: A database developer writes the code that lives inside the database: PL/SQL packages, stored procedures (saved programs the database runs), triggers and complex queries that applications and reports depend on. They work with application developers, testers and DBAs, often in banks, insurers and large IT services teams.
dailyDuties: Write and change PL/SQL packages, procedures and functions
Tune slow queries using explain plans and indexes
Design new tables and views for application changes
Write shell scripts that run and check database jobs
Fix data issues raised by support and business users
Review database code and deploy it through test environments

skills.expectation: Write PL/SQL packages, procedures, functions and triggers
Write complex joins, subqueries and set-based SQL
Develop on Oracle Database, usually 12c to 19c
Use analytic functions and CTEs in reports and reconciliations
Read explain plans, add indexes and tune slow SQL and PL/SQL
Design tables, keys and views for new features
Write Unix shell scripts to run and monitor database jobs
Load and transform data with SQL*Loader, external tables or an ETL tool
Run PL/SQL jobs from Control-M, Autosys or a similar scheduler
Use Python for data checks and automation
Keep database code in version control
Know banking or regulatory reporting data, where many of these roles sit

certifications.why: Oracle SQL basics; the PL/SQL professional exam builds on it
